Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
value.conclusion: dim_H(E×[0,1])=dim_H E+1, with the Euclidean metric on Eucl(n+1).

parameters.type: natural number (the nonnegative integer index of the Euclidean ambient space)

hypotheses.origin: problem.md:21; n is the nonnegative integer ambient index, including n=0.
problem.md:16-22; explicitly approved addition to the printed exercise.

hypotheses.statement: E is compact in the Euclidean metric of R^n.

definitions.definition: For each nonnegative integer k, Eucl(k)=R^k is the space of real k-tuples, with distance (sum_{j=1}^k |x_j-y_j|^2)^(1/2) and its Borel sigma algebra. The empty tuple is the sole point of Eucl(0). Eucl(k)×R is identified with Eucl(k+1) by adjoining the last coordinate; this identification uses the Euclidean distance sqrt(||x-y||_2^2+|t-u|^2).

definitions.type: diameter function on subsets of metric or extended metric spaces
definitions.definition: diam(A)=sup{dist(x,y): x,y in A}, as an extended nonnegative number, with supremum of the empty set zero. Thus diam(empty)=0. In ordinary Euclidean spaces a nonempty set of diameter zero is a singleton. Native ediam is this extended-valued diameter. Euclidean finite diameters are identified with their nonnegative real values.

binders.type: subset of a metric or extended metric space

definitions.type: positive exponent and scale Hausdorff contents and limiting Hausdorff measure on Euclidean sets
definitions.definition:
For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put

\[
H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
 A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
\qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
\]

Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero.

binders.type: countable family of subsets of the same Euclidean space

definitions.type: real exponent → Borel Hausdorff measure on any extended metric space
definitions.definition: muH(a) denotes the native unnormalized Borel Hausdorff measure MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a. It is obtained by the metric outer-measure construction mkMetric with gauge r↦r^a on extended nonnegative diameters: at each positive scale take the maximal outer measure bounded by the gauge on all nonempty sets of at most that diameter, then take the supremum over scales and its Borel-measure realization. Values on arbitrary sets mean outer-measure values. Empty covering members cost zero and nonempty members cost diam^a with extended nonnegative-real powers; at a=0 a nonempty singleton has cost 1.

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of subsets of metric spaces, valued in [0,infinity]
definitions.definition: dimH(A), also written dim_H A, is the standard Hausdorff dimension: sup({a≥0 : muH(a)(A)=infinity}) in [0,infinity], where the supremum of an empty set is 0. This is the native dimH definition. The notation uses the empty-set dimension convention 0. Critical-exponent properties and agreement with the supplied positive-exponent diameter-cost measure are proof obligations, not extra assumptions.

binders.type: subset of an extended metric space

definitions.definition: F=E×I under the Euclidean identification in D001.
D=dimH(E), initially an extended nonnegative real. Real arithmetic involving D is used only after its finiteness is proved.

definitions.type: Lebesgue measure on R and associated integral notation
definitions.definition: lambda is the standard Lebesgue measure on R with its Borel measurable structure and the normalization by interval length. For a Borel set J, |J| denotes lambda(J). The symbol 1_J denotes its indicator, equal to 1 on J and 0 elsewhere. Integrals of nonnegative functions are extended Lebesgue integrals (native lintegral). Restriction to I is lambda restricted to [0,1]. The usual interval values are lambda(I)=1 and lambda((a,b))=b-a for a<b; only these interval values are used.

value.representation_notes: Use EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)=PiLp 2 (constant ℝ), indexed by Fin n, with its native L2 metric and Borel structure; n is a natural ambient dimension including 0. YuiSnoc appends a real coordinate and YuiHead/YuiLast recover it; YuiCylinder E is defined by these coordinates directly in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+1)). T003 checks the coordinate inverse and Euclidean distance identities used by all cylinder arguments, so there is no max-product metric or unproved metric replacement. The interval remains Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1. Metric.ediam, YuiCost, YuiContent and YuiMeasure take values in ℝ≥0∞; ^ with a real exponent is ENNReal.rpow. The supremum over a nonempty witness equals ediam^s and over an empty witness equals zero, giving the prescribed empty-cover convention even at exponent zero. All uses of Hausdorff content or normalization are guarded by s>0 and δ>0. Cover sequences enumerate countable covers with empty padding; the positive-diameter construction uses a subset of ℕ to avoid duplicating finite nonempty families. dimH is native, defined as the supremum of nonnegative exponents with infinite native unnormalized Hausdorff measure; its nonnegative extended codomain gives dimH empty=0. Positive real exponents are embedded by ENNReal.ofReal only with the relevant positivity; D remains dimH E in ℝ≥0∞ and its toReal value is used only downstream of T005's finiteness. Nat casts of n and constants are finite ENNReal values. Lebesgue measure/integrals in the slicing and interval workers are volume on ℝ and the nonnegative lintegral. All five M facts are supplied by direct pinned Mathlib use, not additional premises. Background notes remain optional node-local references. N outputs are unchanged; auxiliary T001 exposes the uniform metric-space normalization calculation already used in S001 so both Euclidean and real-interval instances can share it.

steps.statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (A : Set X) (a : ℝ), 0 < a → YuiMeasure a A = MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a A
steps.explanation: Implementation normalization lemma for the same diameter-cover definition. The proof in S001 is uniform in the metric space; instantiate the generic native hausdorffMeasure_apply both for Euclidean spaces and for the real interval, without introducing a second interval representation. Restrict the native positive extended scales to positive finite real scales by cofinality toward zero. Enumerating countable families with empty padding preserves the infimum. Nonempty-index suprema give zero for empty sets and ediam^a otherwise; at a>0 this agrees with real diameter power on every finite-scale member. No theorem is assumed by a definition.

steps.statement: (∀ (k : ℕ) (A : Set (YuiEucl k)) (a : ℝ), 0 < a → YuiMeasure a A = MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a A ∧ (dimH A < ENNReal.ofReal a → YuiMeasure a A = 0) ∧ (ENNReal.ofReal a < dimH A → YuiMeasure a A = ⊤) ∧ (YuiMeasure a A = 0 → dimH A ≤ ENNReal.ofReal a) ∧ (YuiMeasure a A = ⊤ → ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ dimH A)) ∧ (∀ (k : ℕ) (A : Set (YuiEucl k)), 0 ≤ dimH A) ∧ (∀ (k : ℕ) (A B : Set (YuiEucl k)), A ⊆ B → dimH A ≤ dimH B) ∧ (∀ (k l : ℕ) (A : Set (YuiEucl k)) (g : A → YuiEucl l), Isometry g → dimH (Set.range g) = dimH A)
steps.explanation: Complete N001. For positive a, ENNReal.ofReal a is the exact embedding, not a truncation; apply the native critical-exponent theorems with d : ℝ≥0 obtained from a and its positivity. Keep all four implications. Nonnegativity is in the extended nonnegative order. Prove cover monotonicity and the between-exponents contradiction of S004; for g on the subtype A, intersect covers with A and transport them in both directions using distance preservation, as in S005. Set.range g is precisely g(A); subtype distances are inherited ambient distances. Empty A is included.

steps.statement: ∀ k : ℕ, (∀ (x : YuiEucl k) (t : ℝ), YuiHead (YuiSnoc x t) = x ∧ YuiLast (YuiSnoc x t) = t) ∧ (∀ z : YuiEucl (k + 1), YuiSnoc (YuiHead z) (YuiLast z) = z) ∧ (∀ (x y : YuiEucl k) (t u : ℝ), dist (YuiSnoc x t) (YuiSnoc y u) = Real.sqrt ((dist x y) ^ 2 + |t-u| ^ 2)) ∧ LipschitzWith 1 (YuiHead (n := k)) ∧ LipschitzWith 1 (YuiLast (n := k))
steps.explanation: Shared coordinate implementation facts already used by the accepted product-distance calculations. Fin n indexes the first n coordinates; Fin.last n is the appended coordinate. Fin.snoc, head and last are inverse point constructions including n=0. EuclideanSpace is PiLp 2, so EuclideanSpace.dist_eq/dist_sq_eq split the finite sum into the first n squares and the last square. The numeral 2 is the L2 exponent, not a coordinate count or max-product norm; LipschitzWith 1 uses a nonnegative real Lipschitz constant. These identities justify the two coordinate diameter bounds and the fixed-x interval embedding.

steps.statement: 0 ≤ dimH E ∧ dimH E ≤ (n : ℝ≥0∞) ∧ dimH E < ⊤
steps.explanation: Compactness supplies a positive enclosing box size. For n≥1 retain the grid argument: C depends only on the box and n; for each fixed exponent s>n its cost C*n^(s/2)*h^(s-n) tends to zero as positive h tends to zero, with h also below the chosen mesh bound. Use N001 to get D≤n. For n=0 use the sole empty tuple and nonemptiness, and zero singleton costs. The dimension and n casts here lie in ℝ≥0∞; prove strict finiteness rather than using toReal before it is available.

steps.statement: (0 ≤ dimH E ∧ dimH E ≤ (n : ℝ≥0∞) ∧ dimH E < ⊤) ∧ (∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ → YuiContent s δ E < ⊤)
steps.explanation: Complete N002, preserving T004 and adding finite positive-scale contents. For each s>0 and δ>0 a finite subcover of radius δ/4 balls has mesh at most δ/2 and finite cost; pad with empty sets to match YuiCover. This holds also at n=0. Each scale has its own finite cover; no uniform bound in s or δ is claimed.

Zero-ambient upper branch. Nonempty E in Eucl 0 is the singleton; its cylinder is the appended interval. Equal subinterval covers transported by the coordinate map have mesh 1/N and a-cost N^(1-a), tending to zero for every fixed a>1. Apply N001 to the cylinder and use D=0 from N002. The metric identity is supplied by T003, including its zero-coordinate case.

steps.statement: 1 ≤ n → ∀ q : ℝ, dimH E < ENNReal.ofReal q → ∀ r ε : ℝ, 0 < r → r ≤ 1 → 0 < ε → ∃ (T : Set ℕ) (U : T → Set (YuiEucl n)), E ⊆ ⋃ i, U i ∧ (∀ i, (U i).Nonempty ∧ 0 < Metric.ediam (U i) ∧ Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal r) ∧ YuiCost q U < ENNReal.ofReal ε
steps.explanation: Positive-diameter cover construction with the original scope 1≤n and q>D. This strict comparison forces q>0 because D≥0, so ofReal q is an exact embedding. At arbitrary r∈(0,1] and ε>0, use zero q-content and replace nonempty zero-diameter members by small positive-diameter balls with summable q-cost budget. Keep the other members. Use a subtype T⊆ℕ to index the remaining members; it is countable and permits finite families without duplicating nonempty members. The existential cover is chosen after r and ε, so no uniform witness is asserted.

steps.statement: 1 ≤ n → ∀ q : ℝ, dimH E < ENNReal.ofReal q → ∀ r ε : ℝ, 0 < r → r ≤ 1 → 0 < ε → ∃ W : ℕ → Set (YuiEucl (n + 1)), YuiCover (Real.sqrt 2 * r) (YuiCylinder E) W ∧ YuiCost (q + 1) W < ENNReal.ofReal (2 * (Real.sqrt 2) ^ (q + 1) * ε)
steps.explanation: Apply T007 at the given q,r,ε. For each positive diameter r_i partition I into ceil(1/r_i) intervals and append them to U_i. The finite multiplicity is ≤2/r_i, and T003 gives Euclidean mesh ≤sqrt(2)*r_i. Group the nonnegative countable sum to bound (q+1)-cost by 2*(sqrt 2)^(q+1) times the original q-cost; all powers use real exponents and finite positive diameters. Enumerate the countable union of finite families with empty padding. The conclusion eliminates the private U, indices and partitions.

Complete N003. At fixed δ>0 use r=min(1,δ/sqrt 2) and arbitrary ε>0 in T008. The positive finite cost multiplier depends on q alone, so letting ε decrease to zero gives H^{q+1}_δ(F)=0 and then H^{q+1}(F)=0. N001 yields dimension ≤ofReal(q+1). N002 permits approximating D by the real values D.toReal+1/j; finiteness justifies restoring the ENNReal embedding. Combine the n≥1 branch with T006.

steps.statement: ∀ s δ : ℝ, 0 < s → 0 < δ → ∀ V : ℕ → Set (YuiEucl (n + 1)), YuiCover δ (YuiCylinder E) V → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → YuiContent s δ E ≤ YuiCost (s + 1) V + ENNReal.ofReal ε
steps.explanation: Slice integration bound for an arbitrary original cover V; V, its nonempty index subtype and its diameters do not depend on ε. By finite mesh all diameters are finite. T003 bounds head and last projections. With rho_i the real finite diameter, enlarge each last projection to the bounded open interval J_i by eta_i=ε*2^(-i-1)/(1+rho_i^s). The weighted eta-error sums to at most ε, including zero diameters. The corresponding head slices cover E at each t∈I. Integrate c≤sum rho_i^s*1_Ji over volume.restrict YuiI. Here c=YuiContent s δ E is finite by T005 and volume(I)=1. Apply MeasureTheory.lintegral_tsum at the countable nonempty index subtype with the measurable interval indicators and ENNReal coefficients; only AE measurability of each summand is needed, with no finiteness or sigma-finiteness requirement. Indicators integrate to volume(J_i∩I) and interval length bounds give cost+ε. Neither V nor its projections require measurability. Convert each finite diameter to a real only after its mesh bound; restore ENNReal powers and nonnegative series at the interface.

steps.statement: ∀ s δ : ℝ, 0 < s → 0 < δ → YuiContent s δ E ≤ YuiContent (s + 1) δ (YuiCylinder E)
steps.explanation: Complete N004. For any fixed δ-cover, apply T010 for every ε>0. If its cost is infinite the bound is immediate; otherwise pass ε to zero with this cover fixed. Then take the infimum over all covers. An empty admissible class gives top and satisfies the same conclusion. Quantify s and δ; no chosen cover or interval escapes.

steps.statement: 0 < dimH E → dimH E + 1 ≤ dimH (YuiCylinder E)
steps.explanation: Complete N005. For every real 0<s<D, N001 gives H^s(E)=top. The scale contents are monotone as δ decreases, so their supremum being top means arbitrarily large small-scale values. T011 transfers them to F at exponent s+1; hence H^{s+1}(F)=top and N001 gives ofReal(s+1)≤dimH F. Under D>0 and the finite D of N002 choose s=D.toReal*(1-1/j), j≥2, and pass the increasing real exponents to D. All displayed assumptions stay in the implication.

steps.statement: ∀ a : ℝ, 1 < a → YuiMeasure a YuiI = 0
steps.explanation: Interval upper-measure calculation: equal closed subinterval covers have mesh 1/N and a-cost N^(1-a) tending to zero for fixed a>1. At every fixed positive δ they are eventually admissible and have arbitrarily small cost; take the scale supremum. YuiI is the original real interval, with the usual absolute-value metric.

steps.statement: ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∀ V : ℕ → Set ℝ, YuiCover δ YuiI V → (1 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ ∑' i, Metric.ediam (V i)
steps.explanation: Interval length lower bound for arbitrary covers, retaining the original epsilon-thickening argument. Restrict to nonempty indices, convert bounded real sets' finite diameters to sup minus inf, and enlarge them by ε*2^(-i-1) total width. The resulting open intervals cover I. Apply MeasureTheory.measure_iUnion_le with μ=volume and the countable index subtype; no measurability is needed for subadditivity, while interval values use their openness. Get 1≤sum rho_i+ε for every ε>0; split the infinite and finite sum cases before letting ε decrease to zero. Empty members have ediam zero and do not affect the restored ℕ-series.

steps.statement: ∀ s δ : ℝ, 0 < s → s < 1 → 0 < δ → (ENNReal.ofReal δ) ^ (s - 1) ≤ YuiContent s δ YuiI
steps.explanation: For each δ-cover, finite real diameters satisfy rho^s≥δ^(s-1)*rho; use decreasing negative exponent s-1 for rho>0 and treat rho=0 separately. Apply T014, compare nonnegative extended sums and take the cover infimum. Since δ>0 its ofReal image is strictly positive and finite, so the negative real exponent has exactly the intended meaning.

Complete N006. T015 and divergence of δ^(s-1) as δ decreases to zero give YuiMeasure s I=top for each 0<s<1. T001 instantiated with X=ℝ identifies this with native Hausdorff measure; native critical-exponent implications give dimension ≥s and hence ≥1. T013 and T001 similarly give dimension ≤a for all a>1 and hence ≤1. This uses the real-interval instance of the same normalization proof, without an extra assumed bridge.

steps.statement: dimH E = 0 → (1 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ dimH (YuiCylinder E) ∧ (1 : ℝ≥0∞) = dimH E + 1
steps.explanation: Complete N007. Choose x0∈E and let g:ℝ→YuiEucl(n+1) append t to x0. T003 proves distance preservation; isometry_iff_dist_eq identifies this with the native Isometry predicate, and Isometry.dimH_image applied to YuiI gives dimH(g '' YuiI)=dimH YuiI. Image containment follows from the cylinder definition, and dimH_mono gives 1≤dimH F using T016. These pinned library facts implement exactly the same isometry and inclusion argument as S030; they introduce no premise ports. Under D=0 record also 1=D+1. The selected x0 is private and absent from the output.

Complete P. Nonnegative finite D from N002 is either zero or positive. T012 and T017 give the same lower bound in these cases; T009 supplies the upper bound, so antisymmetry yields equality. YuiCylinder is the subset of Euclidean (n+1)-space with head in E and last coordinate in [0,1], exactly the specified product identification.

1: # Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
6: Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
7: Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
8: Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).
9: 
10: > 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
11: > \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
12: > \(\mathbb R\).
13: 
14: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
15: 
16: Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
17: 2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
18: \(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
19: the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.
20: 
21: Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
22: compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
23: with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove
24: 
25: \[
26: \dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
27: \]
28: 
29: The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
30: formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
31: 
32: ## Fixed natural-language proof
33: 
34: For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put
35: 
36: \[
37: H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
38:  A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
39: \qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
40: \]
41: 
42: Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
43: unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension. We use
44: its critical-exponent characterization: \(H^s(A)=0\) if
45: \(s>\dim_H A\), and \(H^s(A)=\infty\) if \(0<s<\dim_H A\).
46: Conversely, zero measure implies \(\dim_H A\leq s\), and infinite
47: measure implies \(\dim_H A\geq s\).
48: 
49: Write \(D=\dim_H E\) and \(F=E\times[0,1]\). First \(0\leq D\leq n\).
50: Indeed, compactness makes \(E\) bounded. When \(n>0\), a box containing
51: it admits a cover by at most \(Ch^{-n}\) cubes of side at most \(h\),
52: for \(0<h\leq1\). Here \(C\) depends only on that box. Each cube has
53: diameter at most \(\sqrt n h\). For any \(s>n\), the total \(s\)-cost
54: is at most \(C n^{s/2}h^{s-n}\to0\). These arbitrarily fine covers
55: give \(H^s(E)=0\) and hence \(D\leq n\). If \(n=0\), nonemptiness
56: makes \(E=\mathbb R^0\), a singleton of zero \(s\)-cost for every
57: \(s>0\); thus \(D=0\).
58: 
59: ### Upper bound
60: 
61: When \(n=0\), \(F\) is isometric to \([0,1]\). Dividing this interval
62: into \(N\) equal pieces gives total \(a\)-cost \(N^{1-a}\to0\) for
63: every \(a>1\), proving \(\dim_H F\leq1=D+1\).
64: For this upper-bound argument now assume \(n\geq1\).
65: 
66: Fix \(q>D\). Since \(q>0\) and \(H^q(E)=0\), for every
67: \(0<r\leq1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a countable cover
68: \((U_i)\) of \(E\) with nonempty-member diameters

By the coordinate definitions YuiCylinder E consists exactly of the (n+1)-tuples obtained by adjoining t∈[0,1] to x∈E. It already lies in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin(n+1)) with the prescribed L2 metric; T003 proves the source sqrt(dist(x,y)^2+|t-u|^2) identity. 1: # Audit B: endpoint fidelity and checked Lean closure
2: 
3: For the optional [basis route](../../nl0/references/basis.md), this same Audit B
4: checks the conditional intermediate under the frozen basis interfaces. It is
5: followed by b2lean's fresh inspection of the actual `YuiClosed.P`, with only
6: original H and explicitly approved class 4 remaining. Its final receipt binds
7: the compiled standalone source and full actual signature/dependency closure;
8: this intermediate receipt must not be reported as unconditional completion.
9: 
10: The stage-two policy is `endpoint-fidelity-2` (Audit B schema version 2).
11: Its semantic objects are every original external theorem E and the complete
12: final target P. P includes its parameters, quantifiers, hypotheses, domains and
13: conclusion. Accepted NL0/Audit A remains the source authority; B does not repeat
14: unchanged natural-language proof checking.
15: 
16: ## Normal final acceptance and deviation exception
17: 
18: The normal workflow uses `yui-frozen-interface-acceptance-1`. A complete independent
19: pre-proof review establishes source-to-type fidelity for every E and full P and
20: all definitions needed to interpret them. Final native inspection compares the
21: actual exported full types against that frozen contract, checks the exact defining
22: header/pins and semantic receipt, and validates standalone proof/dependency/trust
23: closure. This normal final gate is pure machine work: no additional final LLM is
24: called. It records inherited semantics, not a newly performed independent Audit B.
25: 
26: The actual E/P types include retained hypotheses and quantifiers. Text labels or
27: a source-hash check alone do not establish this gate. The original mathematical
28: review may be wrong; the machine establishes preservation of that reviewed encoding,
29: not correctness of the reviewer's natural-language judgment.
30: 
31: Only complete proof-integrity success plus genuine endpoint/definition drift may
32: open the exceptional independent B-final review below. A faithful result then has
33: `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL`, a freeze-deviation warning and an explicit harness-defect
34: report. Invalid native evidence, incomplete dependencies or changed provenance
35: cannot be overridden semantically. Nonfaithful/unverified results wait for the
36: three explicit user choices in [proof repair](proof-repair.md); accepting a different
37: result does not complete the original target. Explicit/manual legacy semantic
38: receipts remain supported under their original schemas and are not relabeled.
39: Explicitly nonindependent/self-review records remain readable development checks;
40: they cannot grant whole-workflow Audit B acceptance. The same qualification rule
41: applies to supplied Audit A authority and incremental producer/cut reviews.
42: 
43: ## Author correspondence explanations
44: 
45: During interface authoring, provide `endpoint_correspondence`, keyed by every
46: E ID and P. Each entry is `{mode: direct|equivalent, explanation: string}`.
47: Keep it short and useful; do not restate the entire proof or manufacture a
48: line-by-line formalization commentary:
49: 
50: - **Direct:** identify the corresponding variables, hypotheses and assertion.
51:   One sentence is enough when the translation is immediate.
52: - **Equivalent:** explain the mathematical identification or reformulation,
53:   why it works in both directions and which existing conditions it uses.
54:   Point to relevant definitions or checked conversions when needed.
55: 
56: For example, expressing invariance under a finite basis of operators can encode
57: invariance under their linear span: explain the spanning property and closure
58: of a subspace under linear combinations. The review must establish those facts
59: for the actual source algebra/action; the word “equivalent” alone is insufficient.
60: 
61: The postprocessing author carries these notes into each E/P entry in
62: `mapping.json`, checks them against the actual export and completes missing
63: notes for older frozen contracts. It must not change frozen proof statements
64: or bodies merely to improve a note. An explanation is an author's claim, not
65: an Audit B verdict or a formal proof.
66: 
67: ## Semantic responsibility before freeze or at explicit B-final
68: 
69: Read the explanation together with the original source statement and actual
70: elaborated Lean type. Follow the definitions needed to interpret the endpoint,
71: including structure fields that might hide extra assumptions. Check each E/P
72: row, then these four global checks:
73: 
74: 1. `endpoint_inventory_and_scope`: all original E statements and P are covered;
75:    the source version, reviewer scope and inherited qualifications are explicit.
76: 2. `external_statement_fidelity`: each external assumption has the source's
77:    complete mathematical meaning, including conditions and quantifiers. With
78:    no external inputs, record that fact.
79: 3. `complete_target_and_representations`: the entire target theorem has the
80:    same meaning, including every hypothesis. Validate the explanation of each
81:    direct or equivalent encoding and relevant edge cases.
82: 4. `kernel_closure_and_trust`: the actual exported proof compiled, all required
83:    producers and intermediate library ports were discharged, and the checked
84:    root has only the declared external assumptions and permitted foundations.
85: 
86: Equivalent formulations are allowed. Do not reject a faithful encoding because
87: it lacks a particular Mathlib type/name, a separate object for every NL0
88: D node, or a duplicate formal representation. A mathematical source-to-code
89: identification can be checked semantically without constructing an unnecessary
90: second model. If the implementation actually crosses two different Lean
91: representations, the required conversion must occur in checked Lean code.
92: Unexplained equivalence, stronger assumptions, missing hypotheses, changed
93: domains or hidden target assumptions remain defects.
94: 
95: Do not accept an explanation on trust or copy the author's conclusion into the
96: review. Record PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED with specific findings and source/type/note
97: locations. A compiler pass cannot substitute for this independent judgment.
98: 
99: ## Freely available Mathlib
100: 
101: All proved results in the pinned Mathlib environment are available in stage
102: two. Do not compare their names, counts or node-by-node uses with the NL0 M
103: inventory. There is no per-M semantic row, imported-proof whitelist,
104: `calculation_links` ledger, or separate review of implementation N/D nodes.
105: Definitions are examined when they determine endpoint meaning, not for an
106: exact inventory match. Notes from Audit A are optional local guidance, not
107: permissions to use a library theorem.
108: 
109: New interfaces normally use Mathlib directly. An older or deliberately
110: conditional interface can retain M ports; `library_terms` supplies an actual
111: Lean proof for each such port at assembly. These are discharge proofs, not a
112: library correspondence inventory. They cannot remain unproved assumptions of
113: the final export. New external axioms or stronger project hypotheses still
114: require returning to the affected source boundary.
115: 
116: ## Mechanical evidence and limits
117: 
118: ### Compact review materials
119: 
120: The semantic reviewer reads the separately versioned
121: `yui-audit-b-review-view-1` in `review-packet.json`. Start at `/scope` and
122: `/mechanical_summary`, then examine each `/endpoints/<ID>` source, actual
123: inspected type and author correspondence. P retains the complete original
124: target, parameters and hypotheses. The view is a deterministic Python extraction,
125: not an LLM summary or mathematical judgment. It never substitutes a declared
126: expected type for the actual inspected type.
127: 
128: `/documents` identifies hash-bound `source-context.json`, `source-original.txt`
129: and actual `Proof.lean`. Read relevant original and Lean definitions there,
130: including hidden structure fields, when needed to interpret an endpoint.
131: Complete raw compiler, elaboration and dependency records stay in the machine
132: archive; they are not default reviewer inputs. A mechanical summary reports
133: actual checks and exceptions, without populating a semantic PASS. The full
134: dependency inspection remains a program responsibility.
135: 
136: Use `read_task_input` JSON pointers, not guessed fixed line positions. Large
137: containers expose keys and large strings expose `next_offset`. Text reads
138: resume with `next_start` and `next_column`. Serialized read results are at most
139: 32 KiB; follow `has_more` until the needed statement is complete. This pagination
140: limit is not a task time/token/call budget. Unknown calls or modified feedback
141: remain rejected with a specific local protocol fault, not a retryable HTTP 502.
142: 
143: ### Explicit reuse of completed native evidence
144: 
145: `audit_b.py reuse-review <new-directory> --original <old-audit-directory>`
146: prepares a new semantic review without rebuilding or changing Lean. It validates
147: every original input and snapshot, the original native artifacts/output, source
148: and accepted-A authority, environment pins, and the exact historical tool
149: snapshots. The new view and current reviewer runtime are separately bound in
150: `review-reuse.json`; the normal current-build tool check is not disabled.
151: Changed or incomplete evidence blocks reuse. Preserve the original failure.
152: 
153: The new independent reviewer receives no previous B verdict, reviewer history,
154: owner reasoning or other-case material. The receipt discloses inherited native
155: checks and a new semantic review; it cannot claim fresh compilation, an unaided
156: cold whole-workflow success or measured acceleration. Changing proofs or source
157: requires the appropriate new checks, rather than this review-only path.
158: 
159: `audit_b.py prepare/build/check` binds the source, accepted A, contract, plan,
160: proofs, tool versions and environment hashes. Build compiles standalone
161: `Proof.lean` before adding inspection. It checks E/P against their declared
162: encoded types, modulo definitional equality and bijective universe renaming.
163: It does not prove equivalence between natural-language text and Lean.
164: Distinct universes must not be collapsed; changed types or hypotheses must not
165: be normalized away. Source fidelity is established by the bound pre-proof independent review, or an actual exceptional B-final review; this native comparison does not establish it anew.
166: 
167: Inspection follows the actual `AuditBExport.P` closure. No `sorry`, unproved
168: local axiom/opaque substitute or undeclared foundation may be introduced.
169: Local bodies still compile against their own task inputs and the pinned
170: library; every required producer must exist. Assembly, inspection and semantic
171: review have separate recorded outcomes.
172: 
173: Version-1 receipts remain historical results under their original policy.
174: They cannot be silently relabeled or accepted as version-2 reviews. Start a
175: new bound audit when policy, source, code or evidence changes. Pending templates
176: never pass. A whole accepted source plus complete native gates and its bound semantic
177: authority yields `AUDIT-B-PASSED`; a fragment yields at most the explicitly
178: scoped development verdict. A whole source with an actual conditional Audit A
179: can yield `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL` after all the same native and semantic checks.
180: It retains the exact source warnings and never upgrades them to full PASS.
181: Neither proves external publications in Lean or
182: establishes formalizer speedup. Preserve failures and report actual costs.

value.text: Fix k,A and a. For a>0 apply M002 with X=Eucl(k), exponent a and set A. At each finite positive scale r every admissible set has finite diameter, so its native extended diameter power is exactly the real diameter power in H; an empty member costs 0 in both conventions, and 0^a=0. Finite families may be padded by empty sets, and any countable family can be enumerated by N (with empty padding when necessary). The additional scale r=infinity in M002 cannot increase the supremum over finite positive scales: its infimum is at most the infimum at any finite scale. Thus M002 gives H^a(A)=muH(a)(A). This argument is for every a>0.

Under temporary premise L1: a<dimH(A), M003 gives muH(a)(A)=infinity, and F001 converts this to H^a(A)=infinity. Discharge L1, retaining that implication. Under temporary premise L2: a>dimH(A), M004 gives muH(a)(A)=0, and F001 converts this to H^a(A)=0. Discharge L2, retaining that implication. Eucl(k) has its Borel measurable structure by definition, and the arbitrary a>0 supplies the nonnegative-real source exponent in both applications. Universal introduction of a>0 yields the two clauses in F002.

For a>0, if H^a(A)=0, the alternative dimH(A)>a contradicts the infinite-measure clause of F002. Thus dimH(A)≤a. If H^a(A)=infinity, the alternative dimH(A)<a contradicts the zero-measure clause, hence dimH(A)≥a. Nonnegativity follows from the [0,infinity]-valued supremum defining dimH. All these are implications with their displayed antecedents retained, not extra ambient assumptions. Since k,A and a>0 were arbitrary, universally quantify them to record F003, the full normalization and critical-exponent statements for every Euclidean set and positive exponent.

Under the temporary premise L3: A⊆B, every delta-cover of B is a delta-cover of A, whence H^v_delta(A)≤H^v_delta(B) and H^v(A)≤H^v(B), for every v>0. If dimH(A)>dimH(B), choose a positive real exponent strictly between them; this is possible also if dimH(A)=infinity, since the smaller dimension must then be finite. The critical statements just established would give infinity=H^v(A)≤H^v(B)=0, a contradiction. This proves dimension monotonicity, discharging L3 with the antecedent A⊆B retained.

Under L4: g:A→Eucl(l) preserves distances, intersect each ambient cover with A, map its members by g, and use these images to cover g(A). Conversely intersect a cover of g(A) with g(A) and take inverse images under g. Distance preservation makes g injective, and both constructions do not increase any member's diameter. Thus the two H^v_delta contents, and then the two H^v measures, are equal for every v>0 and delta>0. The same between-exponents contradiction as in S004 shows dimH(g(A))=dimH(A). This also treats empty A, whose contents vanish and dimension is 0. Discharge L4 and quantify k,A,l,g and retain each stated conditional premise to obtain every clause of the exported claim.

H003 says E is compact. Compact subsets of Euclidean space are bounded: the open balls centered at the origin with positive integer radii cover the space, so a finite subcover of E puts it inside one such ball. Hence there exists a real L>0 with E⊆[-L,L]^n. Record this existence before choosing L.

Choose L as in F001 and set C=(2L+2)^n. By H001, n≥0; first take the branch L1: n≥1. For 0<h≤1, divide each coordinate interval [-L,L] into at most ceil(2L/h) closed intervals of length at most h. The resulting grid contains at most (2L/h+1)^n≤C h^(-n) cubes, each of diameter at most sqrt(n) h, and covers E. For any s>n the total s-cost is at most C n^(s/2) h^(s-n), which tends to zero as h decreases to zero. At each fixed target scale take h≤delta/sqrt(n) and then h arbitrarily small; H^s_delta(E)=0 at every scale, hence H^s(E)=0. N001 yields D≤s for every s>n, so D≤n. N001 also gives 0≤D. This proves the branch L1 implication; discharge L1.

For the other branch L2: n=0, H002 and the single empty tuple give E=Eucl(0), a singleton. A singleton cover has diameter 0 and zero s-cost for every s>0, so H^s(E)=0 for all s>0. N001 gives D≤s for every s>0, and D≥0, hence D=0. Discharge L2. Since the nonnegative integer n is either zero or at least one, the two branches and F002 give 0≤D≤n, in particular finite D.

Finally let s>0 and delta>0. The family of open balls centered at points of E with radius delta/4 covers E. By H003 it has a finite subcover. Each such ball has diameter at most delta/2≤delta, and its s-cost is finite; for n=0 its diameter is 0. Thus this finite admissible cover has finite total cost, so H^s_delta(E)<infinity. Together with F003 this is the exported claim.

First consider L1: n=0. N002 gives D=0. H002 and the fact that Eucl(0) has one point imply E=Eucl(0), so F is isometric to I. For any a>1, divide I into N equal closed intervals, where N ranges through the positive integers. Their corresponding copies in F have diameter 1/N, total a-cost N(1/N)^a=N^(1-a) tending to zero, and mesh tending to zero. Thus H^a(F)=0: at each fixed delta, sufficiently large N are admissible and their costs tend to zero. N001 gives dimH(F)≤a for every a>1, hence dimH(F)≤1=D+1. Discharge L1.

For the remaining branch introduce L2: n≥1, and fix q with temporary premise L3: q>D. N002 gives D≥0, so q>0. N001 gives H^q(E)=0 and therefore H^q_r(E)=0 at any r>0. For arbitrary r in (0,1] and epsilon>0, the infimum defining H^q_r supplies a countable r-cover of cost <epsilon/2. Discard empty members. Each nonempty member of diameter zero is a singleton. Replace its i-th occurrence by a Euclidean ball centered at that singleton, of positive diameter ≤r and q-cost <epsilon 2^(-i-2). 132: Each summand is nonnegative and measurable since \(J_i\) is open.

134: theorem for this nonnegative series. Since

51: * for a map that is known to be both Lipschitz and antilipschitz (e.g., for an `Isometry` or
52:   a `ContinuousLinearEquiv`) we also prove `dimH (f '' s) = dimH s`.
53: 
54: ### Hausdorff measure in `ℝⁿ`
55: 
56: * `Real.dimH_of_nonempty_interior`: if `s` is a set in a finite-dimensional real vector space `E`
57:   with nonempty interior, then the Hausdorff dimension of `s` is equal to the dimension of `E`.
58: * `dense_compl_of_dimH_lt_finrank`: if `s` is a set in a finite-dimensional real vector space `E`
59:   with Hausdorff dimension strictly less than the dimension of `E`, the `s` has a dense complement.
60: * `ContDiff.dense_compl_range_of_finrank_lt_finrank`: the complement to the range of a `C¹`
61:   smooth map is dense provided that the dimension of the domain is strictly less than the dimension
62:   of the codomain.
63: 
64: ## Notation
65: 
66: We use the following notation localized in `MeasureTheory`. It is defined in
67: `MeasureTheory.Measure.Hausdorff`.
68: 
69: - `μH[d]` : `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure d`
70: 
71: ## Implementation notes
72: 
73: * The definition of `dimH` explicitly uses `borel X` as a measurable space structure. This way we
74:   can formulate lemmas about Hausdorff dimension without assuming that the environment has a
75:   `[MeasurableSpace X]` instance that is equal but possibly not defeq to `borel X`.
76: 
77:   Lemma `dimH_def` unfolds this definition using whatever `[MeasurableSpace X]` instance we have in
78:   the environment (as long as it is equal to `borel X`).
79: 
80: * The definition `dimH` is irreducible; use API lemmas or `dimH_def` instead.
81:

value.text: Fix k,A and a. For a>0 apply M002 with X=Eucl(k), exponent a and set A. At each finite positive scale r every admissible set has finite diameter, so its native extended diameter power is exactly the real diameter power in H; an empty member costs 0 in both conventions, and 0^a=0. Finite families may be padded by empty sets, and any countable family can be enumerated by N (with empty padding when necessary). The additional scale r=infinity in M002 cannot increase the supremum over finite positive scales: its infimum is at most the infimum at any finite scale. Thus M002 gives H^a(A)=muH(a)(A). This argument is for every a>0.

Under temporary premise L1: a<dimH(A), M003 gives muH(a)(A)=infinity, and F001 converts this to H^a(A)=infinity. Discharge L1, retaining that implication. Under temporary premise L2: a>dimH(A), M004 gives muH(a)(A)=0, and F001 converts this to H^a(A)=0. Discharge L2, retaining that implication. Eucl(k) has its Borel measurable structure by definition, and the arbitrary a>0 supplies the nonnegative-real source exponent in both applications. Universal introduction of a>0 yields the two clauses in F002.

For a>0, if H^a(A)=0, the alternative dimH(A)>a contradicts the infinite-measure clause of F002. Thus dimH(A)≤a. If H^a(A)=infinity, the alternative dimH(A)<a contradicts the zero-measure clause, hence dimH(A)≥a. Nonnegativity follows from the [0,infinity]-valued supremum defining dimH. All these are implications with their displayed antecedents retained, not extra ambient assumptions. Since k,A and a>0 were arbitrary, universally quantify them to record F003, the full normalization and critical-exponent statements for every Euclidean set and positive exponent.

Under the temporary premise L3: A⊆B, every delta-cover of B is a delta-cover of A, whence H^v_delta(A)≤H^v_delta(B) and H^v(A)≤H^v(B), for every v>0. If dimH(A)>dimH(B), choose a positive real exponent strictly between them; this is possible also if dimH(A)=infinity, since the smaller dimension must then be finite. The critical statements just established would give infinity=H^v(A)≤H^v(B)=0, a contradiction. This proves dimension monotonicity, discharging L3 with the antecedent A⊆B retained.

Under L4: g:A→Eucl(l) preserves distances, intersect each ambient cover with A, map its members by g, and use these images to cover g(A). Conversely intersect a cover of g(A) with g(A) and take inverse images under g. Distance preservation makes g injective, and both constructions do not increase any member's diameter. Thus the two H^v_delta contents, and then the two H^v measures, are equal for every v>0 and delta>0. The same between-exponents contradiction as in S004 shows dimH(g(A))=dimH(A). This also treats empty A, whose contents vanish and dimension is 0. Discharge L4 and quantify k,A,l,g and retain each stated conditional premise to obtain every clause of the exported claim.

H003 says E is compact. Compact subsets of Euclidean space are bounded: the open balls centered at the origin with positive integer radii cover the space, so a finite subcover of E puts it inside one such ball. Hence there exists a real L>0 with E⊆[-L,L]^n. Record this existence before choosing L.

Choose L as in F001 and set C=(2L+2)^n. By H001, n≥0; first take the branch L1: n≥1. For 0<h≤1, divide each coordinate interval [-L,L] into at most ceil(2L/h) closed intervals of length at most h. The resulting grid contains at most (2L/h+1)^n≤C h^(-n) cubes, each of diameter at most sqrt(n) h, and covers E. For any s>n the total s-cost is at most C n^(s/2) h^(s-n), which tends to zero as h decreases to zero. At each fixed target scale take h≤delta/sqrt(n) and then h arbitrarily small; H^s_delta(E)=0 at every scale, hence H^s(E)=0. N001 yields D≤s for every s>n, so D≤n. N001 also gives 0≤D. This proves the branch L1 implication; discharge L1.

For the other branch L2: n=0, H002 and the single empty tuple give E=Eucl(0), a singleton. A singleton cover has diameter 0 and zero s-cost for every s>0, so H^s(E)=0 for all s>0. N001 gives D≤s for every s>0, and D≥0, hence D=0. Discharge L2. Since the nonnegative integer n is either zero or at least one, the two branches and F002 give 0≤D≤n, in particular finite D.

Finally let s>0 and delta>0. The family of open balls centered at points of E with radius delta/4 covers E. By H003 it has a finite subcover. Each such ball has diameter at most delta/2≤delta, and its s-cost is finite; for n=0 its diameter is 0. Thus this finite admissible cover has finite total cost, so H^s_delta(E)<infinity. Together with F003 this is the exported claim.

First consider L1: n=0. N002 gives D=0. H002 and the fact that Eucl(0) has one point imply E=Eucl(0), so F is isometric to I. For any a>1, divide I into N equal closed intervals, where N ranges through the positive integers. Their corresponding copies in F have diameter 1/N, total a-cost N(1/N)^a=N^(1-a) tending to zero, and mesh tending to zero. Thus H^a(F)=0: at each fixed delta, sufficiently large N are admissible and their costs tend to zero. N001 gives dimH(F)≤a for every a>1, hence dimH(F)≤1=D+1. Discharge L1.

For the remaining branch introduce L2: n≥1, and fix q with temporary premise L3: q>D. N002 gives D≥0, so q>0. N001 gives H^q(E)=0 and therefore H^q_r(E)=0 at any r>0. For arbitrary r in (0,1] and epsilon>0, the infimum defining H^q_r supplies a countable r-cover of cost <epsilon/2. Discard empty members. Each nonempty member of diameter zero is a singleton. Replace its i-th occurrence by a Euclidean ball centered at that singleton, of positive diameter ≤r and q-cost <epsilon 2^(-i-2). Such a ball exists since n≥1, and arbitrarily small positive radii have positive diameter and q-cost tending to zero. Keep the other members. Their total cost is <epsilon/2+epsilon sum_{i≥0}2^(-i-2)=epsilon. This proves existence of a countable cover of E by nonempty members with positive diameters ≤r and total q-cost <epsilon.

Choose U from F002; set r_i=diam(U_i) and N_i=ceil(1/r_i). Partition I into N_i equal closed intervals of length 1/N_i≤r_i. Since 0<r_i≤r≤1, N_i≤1/r_i+1≤2/r_i. Let W be the family of products of U_i with these intervals. It is countable, being a countable union of finite families, and covers F. For any two points in a member of W, the squared Euclidean distance is at most r_i^2+r_i^2. Thus each member has diameter ≤sqrt(2) r_i≤sqrt(2) r.

Using F003 and q>0, the total (q+1)-cost of W is at most sum_i N_i(sqrt(2) r_i)^(q+1) ≤ 2(sqrt(2))^(q+1) sum_i r_i^q < 2(sqrt(2))^(q+1) epsilon. All terms are nonnegative, so termwise inequalities and the countable grouping are valid even before finiteness is known; the last strict inequality supplies finiteness. Since r and epsilon were arbitrary and the private U does not occur in the assertion, this proves: for every r0 in (0,1] and every e0>0, F has a countable cover of mesh ≤sqrt(2) r0 and (q+1)-cost <2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)e0.

For an arbitrary delta>0 set r_star=min(1,delta/sqrt(2))>0. Apply F004 with r0=r_star and arbitrary e0>0. The resulting covers are delta-admissible and their (q+1)-cost is less than 2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)e0. Let e0 decrease to zero, keeping q and delta fixed; hence H^{q+1}_delta(F)=0. Since delta was arbitrary, H^{q+1}(F)=0. N001 gives dimH(F)≤q+1.

Discharge L3 and universally quantify q: for every q>D, dimH(F)≤q+1. N002 makes D a finite real number; take q=D+1/j for positive integers j and let j tend to infinity to get dimH(F)≤D+1 (the previous bound also makes dimH(F) finite). Discharge L2, proving the n≥1 branch. Together with F001 and the exhaustive alternatives n=0 or n≥1, this proves the exported claim.

Fix s>0 and delta>0. Take any countable family V and introduce L1: V is a delta-cover of F. Enumerate it with possible empty padding, discard empties, and write T⊆N for the remaining indices; all i-series in this inference are over T. Define rho_i=diam(V_i), and A_i and B_i as its first and last coordinate projections. By the Euclidean distance formula, each coordinate projection is 1-Lipschitz. Thus A_i and B_i are nonempty and have diameter ≤rho_i≤delta. In particular B_i is bounded, with finite infimum and supremum and sup B_i-inf B_i≤rho_i. Put c=H^s_delta(E). By N002, c is finite.

For arbitrary epsilon>0 set eta_i=epsilon 2^(-i-1)/(1+rho_i^s)>0. By F001 define the bounded open interval J_i=(inf B_i-eta_i/2,sup B_i+eta_i/2). It contains B_i and its length is sup B_i-inf B_i+eta_i≤rho_i+eta_i. This construction also works when rho_i=0. No measurability of V_i, A_i or B_i is asserted or required. Furthermore sum_i eta_i rho_i^s≤epsilon sum_{i in T}2^(-i-1)≤epsilon, since 0≤rho_i^s/(1+rho_i^s)≤1.

For each t∈I, the A_i with t∈J_i cover E. Indeed, for each x∈E, the point (x,t)∈F lies in some V_i, so x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. Their diameters are ≤rho_i≤delta by F001. The definition of the infimum H^s_delta(E) therefore gives c≤sum_i rho_i^s 1_{J_i}(t). Define f_i(t)=rho_i^s 1_{J_i}(t). Each f_i is a nonnegative Borel measurable function: J_i is open and the coefficient rho_i^s is finite. Thus it is almost-everywhere measurable for lambda restricted to I.

Integrate F003 over I, whose Lebesgue measure is one. Monotonicity of the nonnegative integral gives c≤integral_I sum_i f_i. Apply M001 on R with measure lambda restricted to I, index type T, and this f: T is countable as a subset of N, and F003 gives the required almost-everywhere measurability. We obtain c≤sum_i integral_I f_i=sum_i rho_i^s |J_i∩I|. The last equality is the integral formula for a nonnegative constant times a measurable indicator, which follows directly from the simple-function definition of the integral. By F002, c≤sum_i rho_i^s |J_i∩I|≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+sum_i eta_i rho_i^s≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+epsilon. Here rho_i^s rho_i=rho_i^(s+1) also at rho_i=0 since s>0; nonnegative series permit termwise comparison and splitting.

The construction works for every epsilon>0, and F004 has eliminated the private intervals and their dependence on epsilon. If sum_i rho_i^(s+1)=infinity, c≤that series is immediate. If it is finite, the inequalities in F004 for all e0>0 and the finite c from F001 allow e0 to decrease to zero, giving c≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1). Thus in both cases c≤the (s+1)-cost of the original cover, since deleted empties have zero cost.

Discharge L1: every countable delta-cover V of F has (s+1)-cost at least c=H^s_delta(E). Taking its infimum proves H^s_delta(E)≤H^{s+1}_delta(F). This is valid even if no admissible cover existed, when the right infimum would be infinity. Quantify s>0 and delta>0 to obtain the exported claim. No object depending on a particular V or epsilon occurs in this output.

Introduce L1: D>0 and, for arbitrary s>0, L2: s<D. N002 gives finite D and N001 gives H^s(E)=infinity. From the definition H^s(E)=sup_{delta>0}H^s_delta(E) and the fact that decreasing the scale only restricts admissible covers, H^s_delta(E) is unbounded as delta decreases to zero: given a finite level, choose a scale exceeding that level in content; every smaller positive scale does as well.
N004 gives H^s_delta(E)≤H^{s+1}_delta(F) at every delta>0. By F001 the right side is unbounded at small scales. Therefore its supremum H^{s+1}(F)=infinity. Since s+1>0, N001 gives dimH(F)≥s+1.

Discharge L2 and quantify s: dimH(F)≥s+1 for every 0<s<D. With finite positive D from N002 and L1, take s=D(1-1/j) for positive integers j≥2. These lie in (0,D) and increase to D, so the order inequalities give dimH(F)≥D+1. Discharge L1 to obtain the full implication in the exported claim.

For any a>1, the N equal closed subintervals of I, with N a positive integer, have diameter 1/N and total a-cost N^(1-a) tending to zero, while their mesh tends to zero. At each fixed scale they are eventually admissible with arbitrarily small cost, so H^a(I)=0. By N001, dimH(I)≤a for every a>1 and hence dimH(I)≤1.

For the lower estimate fix 0<s<1 and delta>0. Let V be any countable family and introduce L1: it is a delta-cover of I. Enumerate with empty padding and let T⊆N index the nonempty members. Put rho_i=diam(V_i)≤delta. Each V_i is a bounded nonempty subset of R, so sup V_i-inf V_i=rho_i. For any epsilon>0 define J_i=(inf V_i-epsilon 2^(-i-2),sup V_i+epsilon 2^(-i-2)). These open intervals contain V_i and have length rho_i+epsilon 2^(-i-1). Thus they cover I and are Borel measurable.

Apply M005 to Lebesgue measure lambda, the countable index type T, and the intervals J_i. Measure monotonicity and F002 yield 1=lambda(I)≤lambda(union_i J_i)≤sum_i lambda(J_i)=sum_i(rho_i+epsilon 2^(-i-1))≤sum_i rho_i+epsilon. If sum_i rho_i is infinite then sum_i rho_i≥1 already; otherwise let epsilon decrease to zero. The V,rho and T do not depend on epsilon, so sum_i rho_i≥1 in all cases.

Because 0<s<1 and 0≤rho_i≤delta, rho_i^s≥delta^(s-1)rho_i: for rho_i>0 divide by rho_i and use the decreasing power with negative exponent s-1; for rho_i=0 both sides are zero. Hence sum_i rho_i^s≥delta^(s-1)sum_i rho_i≥delta^(s-1) by F003. Discharge L1 and take the infimum over all delta-covers V. This proves H^s_delta(I)≥delta^(s-1) for every delta>0.

Since s-1<0, delta^(s-1) tends to infinity as delta decreases to zero, and F004 implies H^s(I)=infinity. By N001, dimH(I)≥s for every s∈(0,1). Letting s increase to 1 gives dimH(I)≥1. Combining with F001 proves dimH(I)=1, with no missing zero-dimensional ambient case.

H002 supplies a point x0∈E. Define g:I→Eucl(n+1) by g(t)=(x0,t). The Euclidean distance between g(t) and g(u) is sqrt(0+|t-u|^2)=|t-u|, so g preserves distances. Its image is contained in F by x0∈E and the definition F=E×I. N001 gives dimH(g(I))=dimH(I) and dimH(F)≥dimH(g(I)). N006 gives dimH(I)=1, hence dimH(F)≥1. Under the temporary premise L1: D=0, this reads dimH(F)≥1=D+1. Discharge L1; x0 is absent from the output. This proves the exported claim for all n, including n=0.

N002 gives the finite real value D≥0, so either D>0 or D=0. N005 gives dimH(F)≥D+1 in the first case, and N007 gives the same bound in the second. Case elimination therefore gives dimH(F)≥D+1 unconditionally. N003 gives the reverse bound, so dimH(F)=D+1. Substituting F=E×I, I=[0,1] and D=dimH(E), with the Euclidean product identification of D001, yields dim_H(E×[0,1])=dim_H E+1. These bounds apply for every original nonempty compact E⊆R^n and every n≥0, as required.

31: /-- The diameter of a set in a pseudoemetric space as an extended nonnegative real number. -/
32: noncomputable def ediam (s : Set X) :=
33:   ⨆ (x ∈ s) (y ∈ s), edist x y

35: theorem ediam_eq_sSup (s : Set X) : ediam s = sSup (image2 edist s s) := sSup_image2.symm

37: theorem ediam_le_iff {d : ℝ≥0∞} : ediam s ≤ d ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, edist x y ≤ d := by

40: theorem ediam_image_le_iff {d : ℝ≥0∞} {f : α → X} {s : Set α} :
41:     ediam (f '' s) ≤ d ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, edist (f x) (f y) ≤ d := by
42:   simp only [ediam_le_iff, forall_mem_image]

44: theorem edist_le_of_ediam_le {d} (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) (hd : ediam s ≤ d) : edist x y ≤ d :=
45:   ediam_le_iff.1 hd x hx y hy
46:

48: theorem edist_le_ediam_of_mem (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) : edist x y ≤ ediam s :=
49:   edist_le_of_ediam_le hx hy le_rfl
50: 
51: /-- If the distance between any two points in a set is bounded by some constant, this constant
52: bounds the diameter. -/
53: theorem ediam_le {d : ℝ≥0∞} (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, edist x y ≤ d) : ediam s ≤ d :=
54:   ediam_le_iff.2 h

56: /-- The diameter of a subsingleton vanishes. -/

58:   nonpos_iff_eq_zero.1 <| ediam_le fun _x hx y hy => (hs hx hy).symm ▸ edist_self y ▸ le_rfl

60: alias _root_.Set.Subsingleton.ediam_eq := ediam_subsingleton
61: 
62: /-- The diameter of the empty set vanishes -/
63: @[simp]
64: theorem ediam_empty : ediam (∅ : Set X) = 0 :=
65:   ediam_subsingleton subsingleton_empty

67: /-- The extended diameter of a singleton vanishes -/

38: /-- An isometry (also known as isometric embedding) is a map preserving the edistance
39: between pseudoemetric spaces, or equivalently the distance between pseudometric space. -/
40: def Isometry [PseudoEMetricSpace α] [PseudoEMetricSpace β] (f : α → β) : Prop :=
41:   ∀ x1 x2 : α, edist (f x1) (f x2) = edist x1 x2
42: 
43: /-- On pseudometric spaces, a map is an isometry if and only if it preserves nonnegative
44: distances. -/
45: theorem isometry_iff_nndist_eq [PseudoMetricSpace α] [PseudoMetricSpace β] {f : α → β} :
46:     Isometry f ↔ ∀ x y, nndist (f x) (f y) = nndist x y := by
47:   simp only [Isometry, edist_nndist, ENNReal.coe_inj]
48: 
49: /-- On pseudometric spaces, a map is an isometry if and only if it preserves distances. -/
50: theorem isometry_iff_dist_eq [PseudoMetricSpace α] [PseudoMetricSpace β] {f : α → β} :
51:     Isometry f ↔ ∀ x y, dist (f x) (f y) = dist x y := by
52:   simp only [isometry_iff_nndist_eq, ← coe_nndist, NNReal.coe_inj]
53: 
54: /-- An isometry preserves distances. -/
55: alias ⟨Isometry.dist_eq, _⟩ := isometry_iff_dist_eq
56: 
57: /-- A map that preserves distances is an isometry -/
58: alias ⟨_, Isometry.of_dist_eq⟩ := isometry_iff_dist_eq
59: 
60: /-- An isometry preserves non-negative distances. -/
61: alias ⟨Isometry.nndist_eq, _⟩ := isometry_iff_nndist_eq
62: 
63: /-- A map that preserves non-negative distances is an isometry. -/
64: alias ⟨_, Isometry.of_nndist_eq⟩ := isometry_iff_nndist_eq

1: # Lean implementation safeguards
2: 
3: Apply these requirements within the accepted NL0 and the fixed Lean interface.
4: They govern implementation, not additional NL0 detail or a weaker Audit B.
5: Use existing library readers and local checking tools; no separate review
6: model, new premise or mandatory lookup of every familiar declaration is needed.
7: 
8: 1. **Check critical library signatures.** Before relying on a critical or
9:    unfamiliar library application, establish its complete type in the pinned
10:    environment, including explicit, implicit and instance binders and all
11:    side conditions. Read the declaration or check a small typed application
12:    when its signature is uncertain. Do not infer the calling convention from
13:    its name or pass an implicit argument as though it were an explicit one.
14:    A previously checked signature in this context need not be looked up again.
15: 2. **Constrain difficult inference.** When coercions or implicit inference
16:    obscure the intended application, give the intermediate fact an explicit
17:    type and supply the relevant named parameters, such as the set, exponent
18:    or ambient space. Prefer this to leaving Lean to discover those choices by
19:    unfolding large definitions. Routine unambiguous arguments can stay
20:    implicit; explicit parameters must preserve the existing target and inputs.
21: 3. **Check conversions before combining them.** When an argument crosses Lean
22:    representations, first establish a small typed conversion fact, then use
23:    it in the main proof. In particular, distinguish `ℝ`, `ℝ≥0` and `ℝ≥0∞`;
24:    check the conversion direction, nonnegativity and any finiteness conditions.
25:    A conversion is not automatically invertible, and matching notation does
26:    not establish equality of differently typed expressions. Reuse a checked
27:    fact when available. Do not invent another representation, a global helper
28:    requirement or an extra hypothesis just to satisfy this instruction.
29: 4. **Isolate an inference failure.** If compiler feedback identifies a library
30:    application, coercion or expensive inference problem, reduce the next check
31:    to that application or conversion with explicit local types before adding
32:    more proof code. Use `check_auxiliary` in a proof worker, or
33:    `check_lean_types` during preparation when that tool is supplied. Helpers
34:    use only the current allowed inputs and never become new premises. Once
35:    the small check succeeds, integrate the result and recheck the complete
36:    obligation; success of a helper alone does not accept the target.
37: 
38: 5. **Repair after a bounded check.** Native checks have a separate per-call wall
39:    limit, normally 180 seconds, and use the controller-owned 20,000,000 heartbeat budget.
40:    A timeout or heartbeat diagnostic leaves the goal unaccepted and returns
41:    control to the same worker. Inspect the retained candidate and diagnostic,
42:    then check a smaller typed application, conversion or proof fragment before
43:    integrating it. Do not repeat the unchanged expensive candidate or disable
44:    limits to avoid diagnosis. Preserve the target, allowed inputs and proof
45:    requirements; a timeout alone establishes no mathematical gap.
46: 
47: The runtime enforces the per-call wall limit independently of these writing
48: rules. Whole-case and model-stage execution remain unlimited by default.
49: Retain failed attempts and actual diagnostics. Standalone assembly, native
50: trust/signature checks and final machine Audit B remain required.
51: 
52: Before freeze, every complete T declaration must elaborate with exactly its
53: worker parameters, instances and direct inputs. Explicitly supply parameters
54: that their argument types cannot determine; a same-named context variable is
55: not an inference rule. The strict declaration check defines the proposition,
56: without proving it, and rejects unresolved holes and non-proposition goals.
57: `#check` is a useful reader aid, not sufficient declaration acceptance. A proof
58: body cannot resolve a hole in its preceding theorem declaration.
59: 
60: Checked auxiliary propositions receive a `yui_aux_...` name and an explicit
61: application with the existing local parameters/inputs. Reuse these theorems in
62: later auxiliary checks and the final body. The controller retains their actual
63: proof bodies and compiles them into standalone assembly. They are same-node
64: implementation lemmas, not extra assumptions. Read the helper index after a
65: context reset; never rebuild a checked helper merely because a turn ended.
66: 
67: Separate diagnostic printing from proving. `show_term` and similar suggestion
68: output may spend substantial time after the proof tactic runs. If that diagnostic
69: wrapper is implicated, check the same proof without it; only the new successful
70: check establishes acceptance. Do not ignore an unsuccessful process exit. If
71: small helpers pass but a monolithic body exhausts resources, retain the separate
72: checked helper declarations and compose them rather than repeatedly copying
73: their bodies into a growing proof.

56: /-- A function `f` is **Lipschitz continuous** with constant `K ≥ 0` if for all `x, y`
57: we have `dist (f x) (f y) ≤ K * dist x y`. -/
58: def LipschitzWith (K : ℝ≥0) (f : α → β) := ∀ x y, edist (f x) (f y) ≤ K * edist x y
59: 
60: /-- A function `f` is **Lipschitz continuous** with constant `K ≥ 0` **on `s`** if
61: for all `x, y` in `s` we have `dist (f x) (f y) ≤ K * dist x y`. -/
62: def LipschitzOnWith (K : ℝ≥0) (f : α → β) (s : Set α) :=
63:   ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ s → ∀ ⦃y⦄, y ∈ s → edist (f x) (f y) ≤ K * edist x y
64: 
65: /-- `f : α → β` is called **locally Lipschitz continuous** iff every point `x`
66: has a neighbourhood on which `f` is Lipschitz. -/
67: def LocallyLipschitz (f : α → β) : Prop := ∀ x, ∃ K, ∃ t ∈ 𝓝 x, LipschitzOnWith K f t

representations_and_conversion_obligatio.notes: Independently checked the pinned definitions: EuclideanSpace 𝕜 ι is PiLp 2 (constant 𝕜), with distance sqrt(sum coordinate-distance squares); PiLp's function coercion is WithLp.ofLp. Thus Fin n indexes n real coordinates, the 2 is the L2 exponent, and no ordinary max-product metric enters P. Fin.snoc appends at Fin.last n and recovers the first n coordinates at castSucc, including n=0. T003 explicitly requires both inverse identities, the full Euclidean distance identity and the two LipschitzWith 1 bounds (the constant is ℝ≥0). These identify the coordinate-defined YuiCylinder with exactly E×I in both directions. The header defines I as the closed real interval with both endpoints. Metric.ediam is the supremum of pairwise edist and is zero on empties. YuiCost's supremum over a nonempty witness is ediam^s for nonempty members and bottom=0 for empty members; YuiCover imposes precisely union containment and the mesh bound. The guarded infimum over sequences matches countable covers in both directions by enumeration/empty padding; T007's subtype of ℕ also represents finite nonempty families without repeated positive costs. YuiMeasure is the supremum over all positive real scales. The pinned native Hausdorff formula has the same empty-member guard, cost and cover conditions, with positive ENNReal scales. T001 explicitly proves equality after restricting to finite positive scales; the top-scale content cannot enlarge the supremum, and every positive finite extended scale is ofReal of its positive real value. T002 retains normalization and all four critical implications. Native dimH is indeed the ENNReal supremum of nonnegative finite exponents with infinite Borel Hausdorff measure, with the stipulated empty dimension. Positive-exponent ofReal conversions are exact; T007/T008's q>D forces q>0 rather than allowing truncation of a negative q. ENNReal real powers at zero and at negative exponents have the expected special cases: T015 uses a strictly positive finite δ, while its proof treats zero diameters separately. Finite-diameter conversions are guarded by mesh bounds, and D.toReal is used only after T004/T005 proves D<top. T001 supplies the real-interval normalization used in T016; T017 explicitly constructs an ambient real isometry whose image of I lies in the cylinder, so it does not misapply the Euclidean-only clause of T002 directly to ℝ. The header contains concrete object definitions, no proof-bearing structure fields and no definition assuming the target.
